Engine Room Records History

The Discovery

October 22, 1998 // Camden Town, London // "The Underworld"

The Wake in the Bar

It was sheer chance. Ryan O'Connell and Evan Wright had ducked into the basement club just to escape the London rain.

On stage, it wasn't a reunion; it was a ghost story. Origin had once been a massive six-piece art-rock orchestra. Now, only two remained: the singer and the flautist. Brother and sister.

The Signal The flautist stepped up to the mic and played seven notes. Ryan froze. It was the "Safe Harbor" melody—the exact tune Cassidy used to hum to him over the phone during his paralysis rehab in 1991.

The Phone Call

"Cass. You're not going to believe who is on stage. Get Holly. Come to Camden. Now."

The Approach: "The Common Language"

In the music industry, deals are made over whisky and cocaine. Holly O'Connell walked into the pub and broke every rule.

The Order

Holly walked up to the band's table. "Five pints of Cola. And a round of chips."

The lead singer stared at the sodas, then at her. "Are you taking the mickey?" He assumed she was mocking them.

The Truth

"We don't drink," Holly said simply. "We're a dry tour."

The singer's defensiveness vanished. He looked at his sister. "Neither do we. Not after what the London scene did to the rest of us."

The "Mirror Image"

As they talked, the pieces fell into place. Like Ryan and Cassidy, the Origin siblings were autistic. The "Safe Harbor" flute melody wasn't just a hook; it was a Stimming Signal they had written to ground each other during sensory overload.

"I didn't just hear a song," Ryan told Holly later. "I heard family."

The Deal

The "Napkin" Deal

  • 1. You un-retire.
  • 2. Record at The Fortress (Blacksburg).
  • 3. You keep the masters (Clause 88).
  • 4. No Grunge. Only Art Rock.
Signed: H. O'Connell / Origin

The singer laughed. "Luv, we live in Williamsport, Maryland. Just down the I-81."
They were at The Fortress three weeks later.

The Stardust Engine (ERR-001)

Named after the very first song Ryan, Cassidy, Evan, and Tyler wrote together at CPI in 1986—celebrating their shared love of the cosmos (“Stardust”) and the rockets to get you there (“Engine”).
